page.text1: Here you can find some of the projects I have made myself. I created this portfolio in order to present myself and my skills clearly.
page.text2: The projects below, which I created myself, are available on GitHub as public repositories. You can see both the code and the results.
page.text3: If you would like to know more about my work, my commercial projects, my technical skills, the projects I was involved in, and the tech stack I used, please contact me. I will be happy to tell you as much as I can.

actOutsCard.shortDescription: A custom WordPress theme with an event calendar, videos, and login functionality for users.

englishCard.shortDescription: A website for English lessons with different groups. I created a custom child theme, rara-academic-child (the parent theme is Rara Academic). In the theme, I added extra pages and post types for students, a login page, and redirection of students to the right page depending on their role.

formCard.header: Custom Form in React with Vite and TypeScript
formCard.shortDescription: It was a recruitment task for a company. The goal was to create a form without using extra libraries such as Formik. The form was designed in Figma.

bazaarCard.shortDescription: React app ‘Products Page’. This project is purely a self-study case: React, Redux, Context, and Material UI. I created it after learning React, in order to try things out and develop my skills. It is simply an example page for practice.

kamcodeCard.shortDescription: I created and deployed my own website. To build it, I used basic front-end technologies: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Parcel.js. The page is responsive on different devices and has two color theme modes.

portfolioCard.shortDescription: My portfolio shows information about me, some of my own projects, my skills, and my programming path. The page has two modes, dark and light, and is available in two languages, Polish and English.

customersListTable.header: Table with a user list in React and Node (Full-Stack)
customersListTable.shortDescription: A table with a form for updating users. It is built in React with Bootstrap and styled with Tailwind CSS. You can add, edit, and delete users along with their personal data. The backend is built in Node.js with Mongoose, and the data is stored in MongoDB.

blogListCard.header: Blog App – Helsinki Full Stack Course 2023
blogListCard.shortDescription: This is a blog list application developed using React, with React Bootstrap for the user interface. It was created as part of an open online course from the University of Helsinki. The application's main features include displaying a list of example blogs with details such as the author's name, the title, and a link to the original blog. Logged-in users can comment on blogs and like them. In addition, the application has a backend connected to a MongoDB database. Both the front-end and the back-end have been tested: the front-end with Cypress and the back-end with Jest.

wpExampleTheme.shortDescription: This is a custom theme that can be used with the WordPress CMS. It includes default templates for pages, blogs, an about us section, and a jobs section. The front page is fully customizable, so you can add your own content. I have integrated two widgets, for testimonials and for cards, which can be linked to specific pages. Additionally, three columns for links and social media can be added in the footer.

wpAcademicTheme.header: FSE Custom WP Theme with Custom Gutenberg Blocks
wpAcademicTheme.shortDescription: This is a custom theme that can be used with the WordPress CMS and Gutenberg blocks. It includes default templates for pages, blogs, events, and lists of teachers and courses. The front page is fully customizable, so you can add your own content. I created custom Gutenberg blocks for sliders, the teacher list, and events, as well as custom post types (CPT) for teachers and events.

rekLandingPage.shortDescription: A simple website created as part of a recruitment task. The goal was to recreate the Figma design using front-end technologies: HTML, Sass (SCSS), and object-oriented JavaScript.

mtcPage.shortDescription: A simple website created as part of a recruitment task. The goal was to recreate the Figma design using front-end technologies: HTML, Sass (SCSS), and JavaScript, plus Webpack for automation.

actoutsContent.title: Act Outs (WordPress Theme)
actoutsContent.text1: This is a project for a client who wanted a dynamic website for their own business. I decided to build it in WordPress, so that new lessons and events with text, photos, and videos could be added dynamically.
actoutsContent.text2: I built my own theme, which contains:
actoutsContent.item1: A header with a logo and a menu (including a mobile menu).
actoutsContent.item2: A front page with the following sections:

subItems.text1: Gallery slider section (with the ability to add or change 4 images).
subItems.text2: Welcome section with a featured image and text.
subItems.text3: Featured Videos section (displays two pages with videos).
subItems.text4: About section (created by choosing one page). It contains text and a featured image.
subItems.text5: Courses section (created by choosing 4 pages containing videos).
subItems.text6: Holiday Programs section. This section is displayed as a slider. The programs are added through custom post types and contain featured images.

actoutsContent.item3: Four custom archive pages, one for each group. The content is displayed to people who are logged in and have been assigned the right role.
actoutsContent.item4: A page with a calendar. Events are added to the calendar automatically from the event post type. To add an event, the user enters its date in an Advanced Custom Field. They can also set the color of the event and a short description, tick whether the details should be shown as a popover in the calendar, and choose the priority of the events (when several events share the same date). To make this work, I created a WP JSON route, fetched the data as JSON, and passed it to the js-year-calendar function. The calendar library I used is js-year-calendar.
actoutsContent.item5: Footer – the user can add 4 widgets to the footer.

subItems2.text2: An extra widget for Holiday Programs, which can be added to a sidebar. The widget displays only the 4 earliest planned programs.

bazaarContent.title: Products Example Page (React)
bazaarContent.item1: Main page: a list of product cards with a category filter and a price filter.
bazaarContent.item2: Profile page: the logged-in user's details, a client panel in the left sidebar, and user settings.
bazaarContent.item4: Sign-up page: registering a new user through a form with validation.

subItems.text1: Add New Product page: a form with validation for adding new products.
subItems.text2: Edit Product page: a form with validation for editing an existing product.
subItems.text3: Products page: a list of products with edit and delete functionality.

bazaarContent.item6: Basket sidebar: a list of the chosen products with buttons to increase or decrease the number of products, and a ‘Pay now’ button.
bazaarContent.item7: Checkout page: a checkout process with 5 steps to complete.

subItems2.text1: Step one: a list of the chosen products, with a sidebar for entering a discount code and choosing a delivery option.
subItems2.text2: Step two: a form with the details (address fields) and a summary sidebar.
subItems2.text3: Step three: a payment form where the user can fill in their card details.
subItems2.text4: Step four: a summary of the chosen products, address details, delivery option, payment option, and final price.

englishPageContent.title: Flick Through English (WordPress)
englishPageContent.text1: This is a project for a client who wanted a dynamic website for their own business. I decided to build it in WordPress, so that new lessons and events with text, photos, and videos could be added dynamically.
englishPageContent.item1: A header with a logo and a menu (including a mobile menu).
englishPageContent.item2: A front page with the following sections:

subItems.text1: Gallery slider section with a description and a ‘Read more’ button.

englishPageContent.item3: Four custom archive pages, one for each group. The content is displayed to people who are logged in and have been assigned the right role.
englishPageContent.item4: Footer – the user can add 4 widgets to the footer.

customerListTable.title: Customers List in React – full-stack project
customerListTable.text1: A React app in TypeScript. The table is built with Bootstrap and styled with Tailwind CSS.
customerListTable.text2: The backend is built in Node.js and deployed on render.com. The data is stored in MongoDB.

subItems.text1: Home page: displays all the data, which is fetched from the API https://customers-api-sgd5.onrender.com.
subItems.text2: Edit page: a form for editing a single customer.
subItems.text3: Add page: a form for adding a new customer.

blogListApp.title: Blog App – Helsinki Full Stack Course 2023
blogListApp.text1: A React app that displays a list of blogs with their titles, authors, and original URLs. React Bootstrap was used for styling.
blogListApp.text2: The backend of the application was developed using Node.js and is deployed on render.com. The data is stored in a MongoDB database running on a free plan, so loading the data may sometimes take longer.

subItems1.text1: Displays an unordered list of blogs.
subItems1.text2: An ‘Add blog’ button. After clicking it, a form appears with fields for the title, the author, and the URL (of the original blog), together with a cancel button.

subItems2.text1: Clicking a single blog opens the page ‘/blogs/:id’.
subItems2.text2: Displays a card with the blog details, with the option to like the blog or remove it.
subItems2.text3: Comments section – logged-in users can add comments below the blog.

subItems3.text1: Displays all users in a table, along with the number of blogs they have added.

subItems4.text1: Clicking a user opens a page with their profile and the titles of all the blogs they have added.

blogListApp.item5: Pages with forms for logging in and registering a user.
